To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of SAT solvers to check the abstract model and to test abstract counterexamples on concrete models is a viable and effective approach to abstraction refinement, that the use of a single SAT solver for both tasks is possible, and that the use of the conflict graph for the elimination of spurious counterexamples is an important step towards the development of a practical algorithm for abstraction refinement.

(1) a satisfiability-based approach is effective for abstraction refinement, (2) the combination of the analysis of the dependency graph and an effective abstraction minimizer is an effective method to eliminate spurious counterexamples, and (3) bounded model checking is effective for model checking of the abstrac-tions.

the SAT-based approach to abstraction minimization is more effective than the one based on BDDs, that a SAT-based approach to counterexample analysis is more effective than an approach based on BDD-based symbolic model checking, and that a SAT-based abstraction refinement procedure is more effective than one based on a BDD-based symbolic abstraction minimization.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SAT solver is the only tool that needs to be used for abstraction refinement, and the only information needed from the concrete model are simple paths.
we have developed an effective model checking approach for safety properties based on a satisfiability-based abstraction refinement technique that is able to handle large state spaces.
the SAT-based approach to abstraction is very effective for model checking of finite-state systems and it is also very promising for model checking of systems with infinite state spaces.
The main takeaway from our work is that
abstraction refinement in model checkers based on SAT solvers does not necessarily require the use of specialized procedures to refine abstractions.
the combination of bounded model checking and satisfiability-based abstraction refinement provides a very effective model checking procedure that is able to handle complex systems.
a simple and effective model checking algorithm can be implemented by combining the power of a SAT solver with a small set of model checking techniques.
